title: India to Sell Up to 6.5% LIC Stake via Offer for Sale Starting August 4
excerpt: The government set a floor price of ₹382 per share for the OFS, a 10.8% discount to LIC’s closing price, as it works to meet SEBI’s 10% public-float deadline by May 2027.
body:
• India will sell a base 2% stake in LIC via an Offer for Sale opening August 4, with a greenshoe option to sell up to 6.5% of the insurer.
  • The floor price is set at ₹382 per share — a 10.8% discount to LIC’s last closing price of ₹428.50.
  • The sale would raise the public float from the current 3.5% toward the SEBI-mandated 10% minimum due by May 2027.
  • Goldman Sachs, Motilal Oswal, BNP Paribas, and IIFL Capital are managing the offering.

India’s Biggest Insurance Disinvestment Move

The Indian government on Friday announced it will sell up to 6.5% of its stake in Life Insurance Corporation of India through an Offer for Sale, the largest disinvestment exercise in the insurer since its landmark IPO in May 2022. The OFS opens for institutional investors on August 4 and retail investors on August 5.

Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Secretary Tuhin Kanta Pandey confirmed the sale on social media platform X. The government currently holds 96.5% of LIC, and the sale aims to bring the public shareholding closer to regulatory requirements.

The floor price of ₹382 represents a 10.8% discount to LIC’s closing price of ₹428.50 on July 31 — a steep cut designed to attract institutional demand for what could be India’s largest-ever block deal.

The Regulatory Clock

SEBI requires all listed companies to maintain a minimum public float. For LIC, the regulator has set a phased timeline: 10% public shareholding by May 2027 and 25% by May 2032. With the public currently holding just 3.5% of LIC, the government needs to offload a significant chunk of its holding.

A full 6.5% sale at the floor price would raise approximately ₹1,57,000 crore ($18.7 billion), making it one of the largest equity offerings in Indian capital markets history. However, market participants expect the actual sale size to depend on investor appetite at the floor price.

Why the Steep Discount

LIC’s stock has risen roughly 28% over the past year, giving the government room to offer a meaningful discount while still selling above the IPO price of ₹949 (adjusted for the subsequent stock split). The 10.8% discount is generous by Indian OFS standards, where discounts typically range from 3% to 7%.

Goldman Sachs, Motilal Oswal, BNP Paribas, and IIFL Capital have been appointed as the book-running lead managers for the offering. The base offer of 2% guarantees a minimum sale, while the greenshoe option gives the government flexibility to sell more if demand warrants.

LIC’s Market Position

LIC remains India’s largest institutional investor with assets under management exceeding ₹45 lakh crore. The insurer’s market share in new premiums has stabilised above 60%, though private-sector competitors have been gaining ground in the unit-linked insurance space. LIC’s embedded value — a key metric for insurance companies — stood at ₹7.97 lakh crore as of March 2026.
